status: DESIGN ONLY: no dependencies installed and no experiment executed
research_question: On identical original host-side float32 fixture bytes, does USearch's f32 cosine exact/HNSW implementation preserve signed cosine semantics and what are candidate recall and observed cost for this fixed synthetic domain?
scope: Standalone synthetic numeric research only. Fixture bytes are the experiment's original AM-side host representation, not captured AM embeddings or AM runtime data. No native AM integration, graph eligibility, semantic relevance, coding benefit, production readiness, lifecycle recovery, or historical root cause is established. No vendor performance claim is adopted.
known_context: The separate native vector_search.search diagnostic reported distance 2 but similarity 1 for antiparallel vectors, while independent signed cosine was -1, in both tested images. Native exact cosine agreed with host controls. The old 50k index creation failure and historical held-out outcomes remain unresolved; do not rescore or relabel them.

fixed_protocol.larger_gate: Both --large and --smoke-events are required. Receipt must contain an existing complete/pass 1000 event. Review smoke and every earlier failure before authorizing later sizes. No automatic retry, tuning, or rebuild-until-pass. Each invocation uses a new output directory and preserves all events; do not delete failed output.
fixed_protocol.fixture: numpy 2.2.6 Generator(PCG64(seed)), draw int32 uniformly in [-127,128) into row-major N x 64, cast exactly to f32; then draw 8 x 64 queries from the same generator and cast. Size affects query bytes. No normalized-copy substitution; the exact same contiguous vector bytes feed index and independent oracle. SHA256 of each array is persisted in an exclusive manifest before measured operations and results, with seed, settings, tolerance, source/design and runtime hashes. Hashes are run-time preregistered rather than independently precomputed golden hashes; verify against a separately generated fixture if cross-run byte reproducibility is needed.
fixed_protocol.oracle: Per pair Python float conversion of each original f32 value, math.fsum of float64 products, sqrt and signed division. Exhaustive 8*N pairs; no N-by-N matrix and no per-vector copying in timed native build/query. Sort by descending oracle cosine then ascending numeric key; rerank retrieved candidates using the same oracle. Exact and HNSW raw library distance should be 1-oracle cosine within absolute tolerance 0.00002. Tie-aware recall requires every strictly-above-cutoff key and enough keys tied exactly at the oracle cutoff, irrespective of library tie order. The deterministic oracle order is reported separately. This tie definition uses exact equality of oracle float64 results, not the score tolerance.
fixed_protocol.controls: Five original vectors exercise positive, antiparallel, orthogonal, nonunit, and three exact cosine ties. Both exact and approximate searches return all five for key-by-key raw score comparison. A separate five-vector, count-two control has one strictly best key and three tied at the truncated boundary: exact must return the strictly best and any one tied key. Independent input gate rejects zero, NaN and infinity before any library call; this is wrapper behavior, not a claim of library rejection. Control failure stops before the data index build. Candidate domain N exceeds 32; all query result count, uniqueness, bounds, and finite-score checks run before using keys to access original data.
fixed_protocol.outputs: append-only events.jsonl with fsync per event, exclusive manifest, saved index, 64-byte truncated index. Build, save, load, exact, approximate, oracle and reloaded-query elapsed times; raw distance/key lists; per-query exact-oracle candidate recall@10, HNSW candidate recall@10, reranked recall@10, score errors, reload equality, file bytes/hash and process peak RSS. Search timing excludes Python oracle and result reranking. Exact recall 1, valid scores, controls, reload and corrupt refusal are pass conditions; HNSW recall is measured, not required to be 1. Errors after directory creation produce a failure event when possible. Abrupt termination, OOM, process-level native crash or failure before output creation can leave only partial output or no event: retain all external logs and report as failed/incomplete, not success.
fixed_protocol.serialization: Actual library save/restore on its own index and fresh search comparison. Separately, a child process calls Index.restore on a real index truncated to 64 bytes. Exception or None is library refusal; acceptance, timeout or process crash are failures, with child output/exit captured. One truncation cannot prove general corruption safety. No AM lifecycle conclusion.
fixed_protocol.resource_plan: Run one cell at a time. Default 1000 is smoke; 10000 and 50000 require explicit gate. Data payloads are about 0.25/2.56/12.8 MB, excluding native graph, Python oracle tuples, NumPy temporaries, child and runtime. Reserve >=1 GiB free RAM and >=256 MiB free private disk, supervise whole process and child with an external 1 GiB RSS cap and 30-minute wall-time cap; abort and preserve artifacts if either cap is exceeded. Caps are operator-enforced, not hard limits implemented by the script. No assumed runtime or benchmark performance; CPU/network contention, thermal state and busy-host load confound single-trial timings. Capture separate supervisor logs and system conditions.
fixed_protocol.reproducibility_limit: HNSW construction may vary despite one thread; settings and bytes are controlled, but no claim of a library graph random-seed guarantee. Compare per-run raw results, not exact timing across machines.
